title: Invocation shims for cross-SDK function/tool calls with retry idempotency and streaming ergonomics
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement language idiomatic invocation shims across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that unify function/tool schema validation, partial/streaming function responses, and retry-safe invocation semantics. Goal is to provide: (1) a lightweight FunctionInvoker helper in each SDK that coerces and validates user-supplied arguments against model-declared schemas, (2) idempotency and dedup tokens to make retries safe across network failures and streaming interruptions, and (3) ergonomic streaming APIs that surface partial results and function invocation progress with minimal boilerplate. This ticket covers design choices, cross-language examples, and initial implementation for the Python and TypeScript SDKs with an engineering spike for Go ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes FunctionInvoker and validate_and_coerce(schema, args) helpers with tests that cover coercion, missing fields, and extra fields rejection

TypeScript SDK exposes a FunctionInvoker class + types that can be used with streaming responses (EventEmitter or async iterator) and has tests simulating mid-stream failure and retry with dedup token
Both SDKs include example snippets in the docs folder demonstrating synchronous invocation, streaming invocation, and retry semantics
Idempotency token added to invocation metadata and honored by server-side router (integration smoke test passes)
Backward-compatible API: existing simple call patterns remain unchanged for users who don't use function schemas
Design notes recorded in Confluence and design reviewed by PM and DX leads
notes: Decision: prefer explicit idempotency_token in SDK rather than implicit hashing of payloads to avoid nondeterminism across languages
Trade-off: strict schema validation (reject extra fields) reduces silent miscalls but can break lax user payloads; default is strict with opt-out flag allow_extra_fields=true
Streaming: expose both async iterator (Python/TS) and callback/EventEmitter (TS) to match idiomatic patterns; Go spike will evaluate channels vs callback
Retry semantics: SDK will automatically retry idempotent invocations on network errors up to N attempts, attaching same idempotency_token and recording retry metadata in logs
Coercion rules: string->number, number->string only when explicit cast requested via Schema.cast_strict=false; prefer explicit failure for ambiguous types
Localization: error messages include sdk_language prefix to help triage cross-SDK issues
testing_plan: Unit tests for validate_and_coerce and FunctionInvoker across Python and TS. Integration tests: run local runtime with a shimbed router that records idempotency_token usage, simulate partial stream + reconnect and assert deduped side effects. E2E smoke test to ensure existing call patterns unchanged. Add property-based tests for coercion edge cases.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind sdk-2026.03 flag. Stage 1: land Python/TS SDK changes behind feature flag and run canary CLI tests. Stage 2: enable for 10% of sandbox accounts and collect schema validation telemetry. Stage 3: full release with migration guide and examples. Communicate deprecation windows if we change default lax validation later.
